page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture, specifically the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and it relies on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the r8gn.4xlarge demonstrates outstanding memory performance, with its Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block uncached memory bandwidth is strong, achieving 285.68 GB/sec for read operations and 134.17 GB/sec for write operations. Database operations under Passmark also perform strongly, placing in the top 25%. Conversely, CPU-bound tasks such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests register in the average range. Large-model LLM inference text generation is a notable performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10% with 2.39 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64-based Graviton architecture offers a high density of memory resources and strong memory bandwidth without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached EBS volumes, which should be factored into overall infrastructure design. This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, caching layers, data buffering, and high-throughput database operations.
